BAY reported 4Q25 net profit at Bt7,127m (+14% yoy / -19% qoq), falling short 
of our expectations and Bloomberg consensus by 15% and 8%, respectively, 
due to higher credit cost. Key highlights are as follows.  
 
- The impact of TIDLOR continued to affect BAY’ s financial figures as the bank 
consolidated this title loan arm in August, and 4Q25 was the first quarter to see 
the full impact. Therefore, it is still difficult to assess financial performance.  
 
- Asset quality deteriorated, as suggested by rising credit  cost (+24bps to 
257bps). NPL may have fallen qoq to 3.82% (vs. 3.95% last quarter), but given 
that ECL in the balance sheet fell by Bt1b despite rising provisioning expenses, 
it suggests that the decrease in NPL probably involved write -offs rather than 
normal resolution. The rise in credit cost was likely driven by the domestic 
business, as BAY said that this portfolio saw credit cost increase from 154bps 
in 3Q25 to 179bps this quarter.  
 
- The ASEAN business remained weak. Loans expanded (+1.2% qoq) only 
slightly, and credit cost rose to 17.4% (vs. 16.6% previously). Note that BAY did 
not book large impairments like last quarter (Bt2.6b), when it received Bt2.8b 
extra gains from TIDLOR revaluation.  
 
Maintain HOLD  
While it is difficult to assess the bank’s fin ancial performance, asset quality has 
not yet improved much, especially in the ASEAN business. As its major 
shareholder does not appear to demand higher dividends, BAY’s dividend yield 
is not attractive versus peers. Under these circumstances, we do not ex pect 
BAY to outperform.
